title: We Have a Sure Prophetic Word
description: We Have a Sure Prophetic Word in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emanuel Cronenwett wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 120.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We have a sure pro-phet-ic Word, By in-spi-ra-tion of the Lord; And though as-sailed on ev-ery hand, Je-ho-vah’s Word shall ev-er stand.

lines: We have a sure prophetic Word,
And though assailed on every hand,
By powers of empire banned and burned,
The Word still stands the Christian’s trust
While haughty empires lie in dust.
Lo! what the Word in times of old
Of future days and deeds foretold
Is all fulfilled, while ages roll,
As traced on the prophetic scroll.
The teachings of the Word endure:
Blest he who trusts this steadfast Word,
His anchor holds in Christ, the Lord!

licence: Public domain: Emanuel Cronenwett died in 1931.
credits: Words by Emanuel Cronenwett (1841–1931), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
